reviews.comment: This guy does not prepare you for future courses at all. If you dont want to struggle in the future, dont take this guy.

The exams and quizzes are graded very leniently and are nearly identical to the homework, so if you can do the homework, the exams are a breeze. Lectures are extremely boring though. Would not recommend going.

Difficult but very doable class. Dr. Thomas will help you as long as you ask but I recommend asking in class rather than office hours. Exams aren't too difficult and graded leniently. Use answers after submitting first attempt on HW to save time. Do prepare for the concept quizzes.

Thomas cares about student learning and has leniency when grading. The assigned homework will take a long time: do NOT wait to start. Lectures are helpful. Recognize that all of the problems across the class are solved in the same way. He uses vectors for the math, making it easier than other professors. Bad handwriting & thick accent. Good Prof.

very hard to reach outside of class, but lots of TA hours. Thick accent makes it hard to understand what he says at times, and his teaching methods are very confusing and hard to follow. spam Jeff Hanson and teach yourself and the projects are hell. TAs will help but his TA for me had a thick accent too, nice guy tho. use the textbook for practice

Projects were hell. Homework's take a long time, but have unlimited attempts and you can see the answers after the first attempt so pretty stress free if you utilize that. Very to the point guy, gives you tons of practice problems to prepare for exams, which aren't too bad, but do make you think sometimes. Lots of partial credit. Solid overall.

I think he's an overall great professor, taking the time to work out problems and explain them. Homework in this class is sometimes more difficult than the exams, and the projects in this class take a long time. He'll review problems for the upcoming tests and tell you the type of questions you'll see, which are similar to the hw and quizzes.

If you care about the class, Professor Thomas is amazing. He tries to help you as much as he can, provided you reach out to him. Lectures are mostly js working through problems. At first he was too fast during lectures but he actually took our feedback and slowed down. 
His teaching style may not be for everyone, but I personally found it helpful.

This review will be a rant about this Dr. Thomas's handwriting. It is ILLEGIBLE. Imagine sitting in his lecture for 3 hours a week with absolutely no idea of what he is writing or yapping about. Which is why nobody goes to class. He will post notes and solutions to the quizzes that are literally impossible to read and understand. Don't take him.

I had Naveen for 225, 357, and 305. He wants you to learn a lot and he wants you to succeed. Visit him in office hours and you'll see he cares. He definitely is not for everyone. Lectures are sometimes abstract and homework is hard. Grades the tests light (I had a 50 in the class and still made 93 on exam 1) so there is hope for your GPA.
Terrible teacher, does not know how to explain his material. I would not recommend at all.

If you can take someone else for 225 I would. Had to teach myself with jeff hanson. The lectures were very unorganized and example problems were hardly ever done right. Made the class way harder than it should have been.

My review has the caveat that I think the curriculum for MEEN 225 is problematic to begin with, and it needs to be revamped. Dr. Thomas wasn't the greatest lecturer for this class, but he wasn't the worst either. Just make sure to show up and listen, and you should be fine. I've been told he's great for other classes than MEEN 260, so there's that.

Professor Thomas was great at explaining every concept. However, there were times that what he was explaining was unclear. Despite this, he sometimes brought some humor into lecture/recitation and is a great person who cares for his student's education and future. :) Tests are easier than the homework.

He is a little hard to understand sometimes, but he is a very caring professor who explains things thoroughly. If you ask, he will try to explain it in a way that you will understand. Even with the projects, if you ask, he will walk you through the calculations.

Naveen is a decent lecturer, but the content is just boring. Homeworks are easy and have extra-credit but long. There is a semester long series of group projects, which aren't bad, just tedious. Don't procrastinate. The midterm and final are a bit difficult. For them, study the lectures thoroughly. This was an easy class, just don't procrastinate.

Good prof. He lectured with real engineering examples. He cares about concept understanding more than teaching for the exams. However, he was painfully slow with grading. The homework and projects are long and tedious, but As with collaboration. The exams are very generously graded. This class didn't feel too hard, just very time /energy consuming.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Naveen Thomas is a great guy, his lectures were ok for the first few units but recitations for all of the units were invaluable, they teach you how to solve problems efficiently for tests. He is a funny guy with very dry humor which made me go to lecture. Exams were graded clearly and easy. As for the projects... Go to Cope's lectures for help.

His lectures were very informative and entertaining at the same time. Seemed like a really cool guy, he was very approachable. Worked through all the problems you could need to learn the material, and the exams were textbook problems with different numbers. Great professor, I wouldn't take anyone else for 225.

He only reads off the slides word for word. Doesnt expand on the material. There is a lot of math in this course and he doesnt do any examples on how to solve them in class. You basically have to teach yourself how to solve all the problems. 4 big group projects that involve alot of coding. Better off learning on youtube.

Assumes you already know the material. typically have to do the chapter hw to know what he is talking about in class. . Doesnt really tell you why he uses an equation for a problem. Only good thing is that he grades leniently on exams, you basically just have to show equations and make it look like you tried and he will give you points.

Lectures only covered concepts with no examples of how to apply them. Gave us zero review material for the exams and loves to put curveball questions on them. Takes literal months to grade exams and projects. Provides virtually no help on the projects. I taught myself more than he taught me. Worst college experience and prof I've had so far.

I did not receive any exam or project grades until after finals. He only responded to a couple of my emails before I gave up trying to contact him. Lectures were not too bad but they rarely stayed on topic. Lectures and/or recitations were also canceled a total of 5 times during the last 6 weeks of the semester
Terrible teacher, if you can find another option take it. He does not answer emails, does not teach well, and does not grade for weeks. Overall very bad experience. He is going to be my first B.

The professor did not answer his emails. Never fully taught the lesson, would often just expect you to figure out the rest yourself. Thought everyone knew more than they did. Took months to grade. Bad professor, if you can get another one, take them.

Thomas was great for 225. Lectures he kinda yaps but he is very interesting and explains the concepts very well. The exams are long and tough but they are graded super light. Class is easy if you but in effort. Thomas helps a lot with projects and cares about the students, wants you to learn and be successful.

Dr. Thomas is a 50/50. If he thinks you're smart, he'll be lenient on grading, help in OH, and just generally appreciate you. If he thinks you're not the brightest, or even just not trying in the class hard enough (no matter how hard you try), he'll make the course difficult for you. Final was incredibly tough, projects are the only saving grace.

This class was... not it. Naveen's lectures, HW, and tests seemed like they were from 3 different classes altogether. He's also a bit snarky and makes the homework as cursed as possible. On top of that, he takes an abominable amount of points off on quizzes for ridiculous reasons. Easy overall but wow, he makes the course as frustrating as it gets.
Not great. Doesn't respond to questions and doesn't lecture well. Would rather retake Thermo 3x than take another course with this bum.

Professor Thomas can be a difficult professor, but he has also been one of my most favorite professors in college. He cares that students learn more than what will be tested, he connects concepts to the real world, and explains things pretty well. He can be a bit intimidating or sarcastic, but if you show up and try, he realizes your effort.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tried to get us involved, but came off as condescending if you didn't nail the answer. Every mistake got a sarcastic remark, making him seem a bit arrogant. Not sure he meant it, but it kept folks from speaking up or showing up to class. Also, his tests were way harder than the practice ones, unlike other classes.

I took Professor Thomas for MEEN 357 and I highly recommend taking him for this course. He is a very entertaining lecturer and really wants to help his students succeed in this course. I especially enjoyed his real-world anecdotes. The homework and the project in this course are not particularly difficult but can be time consuming.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof. Explains things very well with proofs and theoretical concepts, but lectures are a bit monotonous. Tests were fairly easy and both are structured very similar to the reviews he gives. Always made the class laugh at least once per lecture and is super funny overall. Assignments can be pretty cursed but he does his best to help you out.

His lectures consist of him reading off the slides without ever going through an example of how to solve the problem by hand and instead will only demonstrate how to code it. This is helpful for the coding assignments but makes his tests very difficult on top of the very specific short answer questions that might not have been covered in his slides

Professor Thomas was a good choice for MEEN 225.  He did a good job explaining concepts in lectures and was fairly engaging.  The material for the class isn't difficult, but the workload is pretty significant.  As long as you keep up with the material and pay attention in lecture an A is very doable.

The content for this class was generally easy but the sheer quantity of homework and assignments made this class fairly difficult.  If you do all the homework problems and understand basic physics concepts you should do well in this class.  Professor Thomas did a good job at explaining the concepts and I would recommend taking his class.

He's really good at teaching concepts, but taking him for MEEN 225 is almost battle-hardening because he expects us to do almost everything on our own with little to no help (especially on the projects).

Dr. Thomas is very knowledgeable and his lectures are decent but he was patronizing, expected us to know things we hadn't been taught yet, and gave unclear instructions for the projects. The homework was a lot, but worth the practice. He was disorganized and changed the class structure multiple times throughout the semester. Take Dale Cope instead.

I had Dr. Thomas for MEEN 225 and overall it was a great experience. 225 is a hard course in general but Dr Thomas makes it doable. His exams aren't too bad and he always does a review session for the projects. He is pretty accessible outside of class for any questions you may have.

I had Naveen for MEEN 225 but that course code isn't an option which is weird. At first I did not like this prof, thought the workload was insane, but that's just engineering classes in general. His lectures were a little iffy, but leaves very helpful videos and assigns a lot of work that while hard, helps learn. Plus he rounded my 89 to an A

Love his lectures, one of the best professors ever,  caring and patient towards students, explains concepts throughly. Very accessible outside classroom takes time and helps with any issues faced. Looking forward to more opportunities to attend his courses

his lectures are him just mindlessly going through slides. does not show you how to apply anything he just reads off formulas. his graders grade super harshly and will take off points two times for the same thing. if you try to go to his office hours or ask him for help in class he will just tell you to google it.
ENGR 216 with Dr. Thomas was chill and enjoyable. Honestly the class is an easy A or B no matter what.
Excellent professor. Truely caring and will help you understand concepts. Also very thorough in teaching. He doesn't just teach the material, he is a mentor.
He's good, goes by the rules and if you have any problems he will help as much as possible. He's just straight chill really nothing bad.

I have never EVER worked with python and this class was by far my most difficult. However, Professor Naveen was open to helping and guiding when I had questions. He informs of information coming up and truly cares about the students. Lectures are easy to follow. Ensure to use the textbook if you have never worked with python(Extra credit too).
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He made the concepts very clear and easy to understand.
All of the material was presented in an easy to understand manner.
